**Finding: COMPLIANT — no redline proposed.**

Kubient's §10(a) indemnity plus the §11 procedures satisfy this rule at or above the fallback, and substantially at preferred:

| Element | Where |
|---|---|
| Defend/indemnify/hold harmless AP | §10(a), p0047 |
| Third-party claims | §10(a) "all third-party allegations, claims..." |
| IP infringement | §10(a)(iv) breach of warranty + §9(b)(i) non-infringement warranty (p0033) |
| Breach of law | §9(b)(ix) via §10(a)(iv) |
| Vendor data breach | §9(b)(iii) via §10(a)(iv) |
| Negligence / wilful misconduct | §10(a)(v) "acts or omissions of Kubient" |
| Notice / control / cooperation | §11(i)–(iii), p0054–p0055 |

Two fallback terms are absent **in our favour** and were deliberately left alone: there are no Customer-modification/combination/specification exclusions, and no 3× annual-fee super-cap (indemnification is also carved out of the §7(a) damages exclusion). Proposing the super-cap would have downgraded uncapped recourse, so it was not offered.

Noted in the rationale but not flagged as deviations: "affiliates" are not expressly listed among indemnified parties; there is no procure/modify/replace/refund ladder; and AP's §10(b) indemnity runs broader than the preferred content-plus-breach-of-law limit. These are sub-preferred points to raise commercially if the agreement is reopened, not a fallback failure.
